findings.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — One failed SendGrid cancel throws out of the shared try, so the remaining cancelled reminders are never cancelled and their emails still go out for cancelled bookings.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row, so the DB keeps a scheduled=true reminder pointing at a dead batch.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — Reminders are cancelled before eventManager.reschedule and the booking write, so if the reschedule fails the original booking has lost its reminders.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — The async delete calls are not awaited inside forEach, so the try/catch never catches their rejections and the handler can return before the cancel or DB writes finish.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:486 — Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget and left out of the awaited prismaPromises, so a serverless response can finish before reminders are flagged, cancelled or deleted, and SMS or email still sends.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:231 — A cancelled email reminder only has its SendGrid batch cancelled within an hour of send time, so a missed or late cron run (SendGrid needs cancellation about 10 minutes ahead) still sends to cancelled bookings.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — New `immediateDelete` branch cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes the WorkflowReminder row, diverging from the SMS helper and the name's contract, so handleNewBooking reschedule leaves orphaned reminder rows on the old booking.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder signature/semantics changed so that without the flag it only soft-flags `cancelled=true` (deferred cron cancel) while deleteScheduledSMSReminder hard-deletes, giving the two sibling helpers inconsistent contracts for identical call sites.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — activeOn update mutation (and bookings.tsx:488 reschedule) no longer awaits reminder cleanup, so the tRPC response resolves before DB deletes/cancels finish and failures are silently swallowed.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:214 — Immediate-cancel path dropped the follow-up `DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/{batch_id}` call, leaving cancelled batch records in SendGrid unlike the previous behavior.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes the WorkflowReminder row, leaving orphaned "scheduled" reminders (e.g. on the old booking after reschedule in handleNewBooking).

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — The try/catch wraps the whole cancel loop, so one failing SendGrid cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and skips deleting rows already cancelled (their deletes are never awaited), so the same failure repeats on every run.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:46 — Cancelled reminders only get a SendGrid cancel when the cron runs inside the final hour before send, and rows past their scheduledDate are purged first, so a missed or late cron run lets emails go out for cancelled/rescheduled bookings.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch around forEach with un-awaited async delete calls catches nothing, and the reschedule path uses immediateDelete while bookings.tsx reschedule uses soft-cancel, so the two reschedule paths behave differently.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but never deletes or marks the WorkflowReminder row cancelled, leaving orphaned scheduled=true rows for the rescheduled booking.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single SendGrid failure in the cancel loop aborts before Promise.all, so no cancelled=true rows are deleted and they accumulate/retry indefinitely (row cleanup is all-or-nothing with no per-row handling).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:576 — The EMAIL/SMS dispatch-to-delete-helper block is copy-pasted across 7 call sites (workflows.tsx x4, bookings.tsx:489, handleCancelBooking.ts:487, handleNewBooking.ts:967) instead of a single deleteWorkflowReminder(reminder) helper, and the call sites already disagree on the immediateDelete flag.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel request is duplicated inline in the cron handler rather than reusing the email reminder manager, so knowledge of the cancel API is split across two modules.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — The email and SMS delete helpers now have asymmetric contracts (email soft-cancels or skips DB cleanup; SMS always hard-deletes the row) behind near-identical signatures, which leaks provider details to callers.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:9 — Prisma` is now imported as a value import but is not used anywhere in the file (dead import); the imports were also switched from `import type` to value imports for no reason.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1 — Type-only imports (App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput, Prisma) were folded into a value import, which undoes the previous `import type` split.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:903 — The commented-out legacy block had its indentation stripped, which adds churn to dead code that should be removed instead.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — Cron findMany of cancelled reminders is unbounded (no take/pagination, lte includes all past rows) and materializes every backlog row per run.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — SendGrid cancel calls are awaited serially per reminder inside the loop, so cron latency grows linearly and can time out on large backlogs.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — A single failed cancel request aborts the whole try block before any queued deletes run, so the cancelled backlog is never drained and gets refetched and re-called every run.
packages/prisma/schema.prisma:643 — New cron filter on cancelled+scheduledDate has no supporting index, forcing a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron invocation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — Disabling event types now fires one unawaited per-reminder DB update/delete (N+1) across all bookings instead of a single batched updateMany/deleteMany.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — A single try wraps the whole cancel loop, so one failed SendGrid cancel (e.g. already-sent/invalid batch) aborts all remaining cancellations and their deletes, and the poison row recurs every run, blocking cancellation indefinitely.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:223 — Cancelled bookings now only set cancelled=true and rely on the cron to cancel within a 1-hour window, so a booking cancelled shortly before a reminder (or a missed/failed cron run) still sends the email, unlike the previous immediate SendGrid cancel.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:34 — The cron deletes all past-dated email reminders before the cancel pass, so cancelled reminders that were not cancelled in SendGrid before their send time are dropped without any cancel attempt or record.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach of unawaited async deletes, so it catches nothing and the reminder cancellations are fire-and-forget during the reschedule request.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488 — Reminder cancellation was previously awaited via Promise.all but is now fire-and-forget (unawaited promises), so it can be lost if the serverless handler finishes first, and failures are only console-logged.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:486 — Reminder deletion used to go into the awaited prismaPromises batch but is now unawaited fire-and-forget, so errors are silently swallowed and the work may not finish before the response.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row, leaving a stale scheduled reminder attached to the rescheduled booking.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder now has three branches (null referenceId delete, immediateDelete cancel, soft-cancel flag) with no unit tests covering any of them.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43 — New cron cancel-and-delete loop for cancelled reminders is untested, including the edge case where one SendGrid failure aborts deletion of all remaining reminders.
packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — Reschedule path now cancels the previous booking's workflow reminders but no test checks that old reminders get cancelled or removed.
packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:485 — Cancellation no longer deletes reminder rows directly and relies on unawaited helpers, and no test covers the resulting DB state.
packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — deleteScheduledSMSReminder now deletes the DB row and skips Twilio when referenceId is null, but neither path is tested.
packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — New nullable cancelled column has no test showing the SMS cron or other readers ignore cancelled=true reminders.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — Workflow update/delete flows changed from direct deleteMany (scoped to ctx.user) to helper calls, and there are no tests for reminder cleanup or the ownership scoping.

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — One failed SendGrid cancel throws out of the shared try, so the remaining cancelled reminders are never cancelled and their emails still go out for cancelled bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try` (lines added around the `client.request` cancel + `prisma.workflowReminder.delete`). If `client.request(...)` throws for any one reminder, control jumps to the `catch`, aborting the loop and skipping cancellation/deletion for the remaining `remindersToCancel`, so some cancelled reminders may remain active and still send.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:74 — The lazy Prisma delete promises only run after the whole loop, so any mid-loop error means none of the already-cancelled rows are deleted and they are retried on every cron run.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, deletes are accumulated in `workflowRemindersToDelete` and only executed via `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the `for ... of` loop. Because the whole loop + `Promise.all` is wrapped in a single `try`, any error thrown mid-loop (e.g., `client.request` failing for one reminder) jumps to `catch` before reaching `Promise.all`, so previously-collected delete operations are never awaited/executed. This can leave already-cancelled reminders in the DB and cause them to be picked up again on subsequent cron runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row, so the DB keeps a scheduled=true reminder pointing at a dead batch.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — Reminders are cancelled before eventManager.reschedule and the booking write, so if the reschedule fails the original booking has lost its reminders.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, within `if (originalRescheduledBooking?.uid)`, the PR adds a `try` block that iterates `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` and calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` *before* calling `eventManager.reschedule(...)`. From the diff, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` always deletes the `workflowReminder` row via `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` regardless of whether the subsequent reschedule succeeds. Therefore, if `eventManager.reschedule` (or the following booking update) fails, the previous booking’s reminders—at least SMS ones—have already been removed/cancelled, matching the finding’s risk of losing reminders on failure.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the loop now calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) / deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) but does not await or collect the returned Promises, and prismaPromises no longer includes any reminder-related operations (it is now only [attendeeDeletes, bookingReferenceDeletes]). Since the handler only awaits Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)), reminder cancellation/DB updates can still be in-flight when the request finishes, meaning reminders may not be marked cancelled/deleted in time (or at all in a serverless early-termination scenario).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:231 — A cancelled email reminder only has its SendGrid batch cancelled within an hour of send time, so a missed or late cron run (SendGrid needs cancellation about 10 minutes ahead) still sends to cancelled bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` no longer cancels the SendGrid scheduled send for most call sites (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `viewer/bookings.tsx`, `viewer/workflows.tsx` call it without `immediateDelete`), and instead just sets `WorkflowReminder.cancelled = true` in Prisma. Actual SendGrid cancellation now happens later in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, but only for reminders with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. This means a cancelled booking can still send an email reminder if the `scheduleEmailReminders` job is missed/late or doesn’t run before the send time, because the external scheduled send remains active until that later sweep.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — New `immediateDelete` branch cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes the WorkflowReminder row, diverging from the SMS helper and the name's contract, so handleNewBooking reschedule leaves orphaned reminder rows on the old booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` has an `immediateDelete` branch that cancels the SendGrid batch (`/v3/user/scheduled_sends` POST cancel) and then `return`s without either deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or marking it `cancelled`. This differs from the non-immediate path (which sets `cancelled: true`) and from `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (which deletes the row). The diff also removes the prior Prisma `deleteMany` cleanup in callers (e.g., `handleNewBooking` reschedule calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`), so the old booking’s email reminders can remain persisted as non-cancelled rows, i.e., orphaned relative to the previous behavior/name contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder signature/semantics changed so that without the flag it only soft-flags `cancelled=true` (deferred cron cancel) while deleteScheduledSMSReminder hard-deletes, giving the two sibling helpers inconsistent contracts for identical call sites.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an intentional contract divergence between sibling helpers: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` now *soft-cancels* by `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` when `immediateDelete` is not set (and does not cancel the external scheduled send), while `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` still cancels (if `referenceId`) and then hard-deletes the DB row. Call sites were updated to call both helpers without the email `immediateDelete` flag in many places (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, parts of `workflows.tsx`), so identical-looking “delete” call sites now have different persistence/side-effect semantics. This inconsistency is real and diff-grounded; whether it’s a defect depends on intended behavior (email cancellation is deferred via the new cancellation logic in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`), so it’s better classified as a non-bug review concern about API/contract clarity/consistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — activeOn update mutation (and bookings.tsx:488 reschedule) no longer awaits reminder cleanup, so the tRPC response resolves before DB deletes/cancels finish and failures are silently swallowed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes awaited Prisma deletions and does not await the new async reminder-cancel helpers. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` (around the “cancel workflow reminders…” blocks, incl. the activeOn disable path previously `await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)`), it now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside `forEach` without `await` and removes the `Promise.all(...)` that ensured completion. Similarly in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` reschedule path it removes `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` and also calls the async cancel helpers without awaiting. Since these helpers perform DB writes (`prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete`) and external cancels, the tRPC handler can return before cleanup finishes, and errors are only logged/swallowed inside the helpers’ try/catch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:214 — Immediate-cancel path dropped the follow-up `DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/{batch_id}` call, leaving cancelled batch records in SendGrid unlike the previous behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` previously did both a POST to cancel and then a `DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/{referenceId}`. In the new implementation, when `immediateDelete` is true it only performs the POST cancel and returns early (no follow-up DELETE), so the finding about dropped DELETE behavior is accurate. However, whether leaving canceled SendGrid batch records is a *defect* cannot be verified from the diff alone (it may be an intentional change, especially given the new cancellation/cleanup logic added elsewhere), so this is best treated as a concrete behavioral/cleanup concern rather than a provable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — The try/catch wraps the whole cancel loop, so one failing SendGrid cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and skips deleting rows already cancelled (their deletes are never awaited), so the same failure repeats on every run.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:46 — Cancelled reminders only get a SendGrid cancel when the cron runs inside the final hour before send, and rows past their scheduledDate are purged first, so a missed or late cron run lets emails go out for cancelled/rescheduled bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the new cancellation logic only issues the SendGrid cancel request for reminders where `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. Separately, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` (when not `immediateDelete`) only marks the DB row as `cancelled` (no SendGrid API call). That means cancellations for bookings/reschedules can depend on this cron endpoint running on time to actually cancel in SendGrid; if it runs late/not at all, a cancelled reminder could remain scheduled in SendGrid. The finding’s claim about "rows past their scheduledDate are purged first" is not shown in the diff, but the cron-timing dependency is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch around forEach with un-awaited async delete calls catches nothing, and the reschedule path uses immediateDelete while bookings.tsx reschedule uses soft-cancel, so the two reschedule paths behave differently.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new cancellation block wraps a synchronous forEach that calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting; a try/catch around that loop won’t catch async failures (and the calls may run in the background). Also, the reschedule path here calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) (immediateDelete) while the bookings router reschedule path calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) (soft-cancel via `cancelled: true`), so the two reschedule flows now behave differently for email reminders. This is a concrete inconsistency/robustness issue visible in the diff, though the diff alone can’t prove it causes a user-visible failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but never deletes or marks the WorkflowReminder row cancelled, leaving orphaned scheduled=true rows for the rescheduled booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early on the `immediateDelete` branch after canceling at SendGrid (`POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` with `status: "cancel"`), without updating the DB row (`cancelled: true`) or deleting it. Since other code paths now rely on DB state (e.g., `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only finds reminders where `cancelled: true` to cancel/delete), this leaves the `WorkflowReminder` row untouched (and likely still `scheduled=true`) and therefore orphaned. The diff also shows callers using `immediateDelete=true` for reschedule cleanup (`handleNewBooking.ts`), workflow deletion, and step deletion, so the problematic path is exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single SendGrid failure in the cancel loop aborts before Promise.all, so no cancelled=true rows are deleted and they accumulate/retry indefinitely (row cleanup is all-or-nothing with no per-row handling).

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire loop + deletion in a single `try`. Inside the `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop it `await`s `client.request(...)` (SendGrid cancel). If any one request throws, control jumps to `catch`, and the code never reaches `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. Since `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` returns a PrismaPromise that is only executed when awaited, none of the queued deletes are executed in that failure case, leaving `cancelled=true` rows in the DB to be re-selected on subsequent runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:576 — The EMAIL/SMS dispatch-to-delete-helper block is copy-pasted across 7 call sites (workflows.tsx x4, bookings.tsx:489, handleCancelBooking.ts:487, handleNewBooking.ts:967) instead of a single deleteWorkflowReminder(reminder) helper, and the call sites already disagree on the immediateDelete flag.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows repeated, copy-pasted dispatch logic across multiple call sites: e.g. workflows.tsx (at least in the blocks around deleting workflows, disabling event types, deleting steps, editing steps), bookings.tsx reschedule cancellation loop, handleCancelBooking.ts cancellation loop, and handleNewBooking.ts reschedule cleanup loop. Each repeats `if (reminder.method === EMAIL) ... else if SMS ...`. The call sites also differ on the `immediateDelete` flag passed to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)`: some pass `true` (handleNewBooking.ts; workflows.tsx for deleted workflow/step), while others omit it (handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx for other cases). This is a concrete maintainability/consistency issue introduced/expanded by the change, but not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:200 — Boolean `immediateDelete` flag switches deleteScheduledEmailReminder between three unrelated behaviors (DB delete, SendGrid cancel without DB cleanup, soft-mark cancelled), so the "delete" name misrepresents what most paths do.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — Cron findMany of cancelled reminders is unbounded (no take/pagination, lte includes all past rows) and materializes every backlog row per run.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the newly added `remindersToCancel` query uses `findMany` with `where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour").toISOString() } }` and no `take`/pagination or lower bound. This can select an arbitrarily large set of rows (including all historical cancelled reminders with `scheduledDate` in the past) and materialize them every cron run, which is a concrete scalability/performance concern introduced by the diff, even if not an immediate functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — SendGrid cancel calls are awaited serially per reminder inside the loop, so cron latency grows linearly and can time out on large backlogs.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts, the new cancellation block iterates `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` and does `await client.request(...)` inside the loop, which makes SendGrid cancel requests run serially. Only the Prisma deletes are batched via `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` afterward. This can increase cron/job runtime linearly with backlog size and is a concrete performance/operational concern introduced by the diff, not a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — A single failed cancel request aborts the whole try block before any queued deletes run, so the cancelled backlog is never drained and gets refetched and re-called every run.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the cancellation+deletion is wrapped in a single `try` with a `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...); workflowRemindersToDelete.push(prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)); } await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete);`. If any `await client.request` throws, control jumps to `catch` and the function never reaches `Promise.all(...)`, so none of the queued Prisma deletes execute. Those `cancelled: true` reminders remain in the DB and will be refetched and retried on subsequent runs, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:643 — New cron filter on cancelled+scheduledDate has no supporting index, forcing a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron invocation.

The Prisma schema change only adds `cancelled Boolean?` and shows no accompanying `@@index`/`@index` on `cancelled` and/or `scheduledDate` in the shown hunk, so this can become an avoidable performance hotspot. However, the diff does not show the full `WorkflowReminder` model (including any existing indexes), so it’s not fully verifiable that no supporting index exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — Disabling event types now fires one unawaited per-reminder DB update/delete (N+1) across all bookings instead of a single batched updateMany/deleteMany.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — A single try wraps the whole cancel loop, so one failed SendGrid cancel (e.g. already-sent/invalid batch) aborts all remaining cancellations and their deletes, and the poison row recurs every run, blocking cancellation indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new cancellation logic wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try`/`catch`. If `client.request(...)` throws for one reminder (e.g., invalid/already-processed `batch_id`), execution jumps to the `catch` and the loop stops, so subsequent reminders are not canceled and none of their corresponding `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises are queued/awaited. The failing reminder row is also not deleted, so it will be re-selected on the next run and can repeatedly abort processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach of unawaited async deletes, so it catches nothing and the reminder cancellations are fire-and-forget during the reschedule request.
